newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, U.S. making progress on NATO deal - Albright.
newsitem.headline: Russia, U.S. making progress on NATO deal - Albright.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Friday the United States and Russia had made "very important progress" towards an agreement between Moscow and NATO on European security.
But, speaking at a news conference after two days of talks with Russian officials, she said some very complex questions remained as NATO prepared to expand eastwards.
"I think that we have made some very important progress on this," she said, asked about a document which would define a new relationship between NATO and Russia in the post Cold War world.
Russia has warned NATO that its plans to grant membership to some of Moscow's Cold War allies in central and eastern Europe could upset the European security balance.
But after NATO made clear it would not change its plans to cope with Russian objections, Moscow has concentrated on negotiating a deal which would guarantee its security interests.
It remained unclear on Friday to what extent the two sides have agreed on the precise form of a future deal.
Russian Foreign Ministger Yevgeny Primakov told the same news conference the two sides had agreed that the document to be signed by Russia and NATO must have a "mandatory or binding nature".
But Albright did not address this point, and it was uncertain if the U.S. had agreed to it. If it had, this would be a substantial concession by Washington.
Moscow has long said the deal should be binding and should include a NATO promise not to deploy nuclear forces and foreign troops on the territories of the new members.
U.S. officials have said relations between Russia and NATO could be laid down in a non-binding charter.
They have also said the document could not include provisions which would curb any rights of the new members.
Primakov said Russia was doing everything it could to "minimise the negative consequences" of NATO's expansion plans.
